base64-encoder-decoder.quickAnswer: Base64 turns binary data into plain ASCII text using 64 safe characters (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, +, /). For example, "Hello" encodes to "SGVsbG8=". Paste text and pick Encode, or paste Base64 and pick Decode - invalid input shows a clear error instead of garbage.
keyFacts: Base64 output uses only A-Z, a-z, 0-9, plus (+), slash (/), and equals (=) as padding.
Encoded output is about 33% larger than the input - 3 bytes become 4 characters.
Base64 is an encoding, not encryption. Anyone can decode it; it provides zero secrecy.
Padding with = makes the length a multiple of 4. One or two = signs may appear at the end.
This tool handles full Unicode correctly by encoding text as UTF-8 bytes first - many simple tools corrupt non-English text.
Common uses: embedding images in HTML/CSS, email attachments (MIME), API tokens, and data URLs.

base64-encoder-decoder.formula:
Encoding: every 3 input bytes (24 bits) are split into four 6-bit groups; each group maps to one of 64 characters.
Decoding reverses the process. Padding: input length mod 3 = 1 → two "="; = 2 → one "=".
base64-encoder-decoder.workedExample:
Encode "Hello":
1. UTF-8 bytes: 72 101 108 108 111.
2. Grouped into 6-bit chunks and mapped: S G V s b G 8 =.
3. Result: "SGVsbG8=".
Decode "SmF1clRvb2xz":
1. Split into 6-bit values and regroup into bytes.
2. Bytes spell: J a u r T o o l s.
3. Result: "JaurTools".

faqs.a: Base64 represents binary data as plain text. It is used in email attachments, embedding images directly in HTML or CSS (data URLs), JWT tokens, and anywhere binary bytes must travel through text-only channels.
No. Base64 is an encoding, not encryption - anyone can decode it instantly with no key. Never use it to hide passwords or secrets; it only changes how data looks, not who can read it.

faqs.q: Why does my Base64 end with = signs?
faqs.a: The = characters are padding. Base64 works in groups of 3 bytes → 4 characters. If your input is not a multiple of 3 bytes, padding fills the gap: one = for a 1-byte shortfall pattern, two = for the other case.

faqs.q: Why is Base64 output longer than the input?
faqs.a: Each 3 bytes of input become 4 characters of output, so the result is roughly 33% larger. This size cost is the trade-off for text-safe representation.

faqs.q: Can Base64 handle Hindi or Arabic text?
faqs.a: Yes - this tool first converts your text to UTF-8 bytes, then encodes those bytes. Simple tools that skip the UTF-8 step corrupt non-English characters; this one does not.
It means the input contains characters outside the Base64 alphabet, or has wrong padding/length. Check for stray spaces, line breaks, or missing = padding at the end.
